cohort: The study included women who had an unassisted, singleton, cephalic vaginal birth at term with a midwife or midwifery student accoucheur in Australian maternity care facilities during two periods: January 2011 - November 2017 (pre-implementation) and August 2018 - August 2020 (post-implementation).
finding: The implementation of the perineal bundle demonstrated no significant difference in the likelihood of severe perineal trauma, but nulliparous women were more likely to receive an episiotomy and multiparous women to suffer a second-degree tear after implementation.
